input.question: Who composed the musical setting for the Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom?

documents.text: Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom (Leontovych) The Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom (, tr. "Liturhiya Ivana Zlatoustoho") is the musical setting of the Divine Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom by Mykola Leontovych. Consistent with Orthodox tradition, in which service is sung exclusively a cappella, the piece is set for unaccompanied choir and soloist. It was first performed in the Mykolaiv Cathedral at the Kiev Pechersk Lavra on May 22, 1919, with Leontovych himself conducting. The Divine Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom is the most commonly performed liturgy in the Eastern Church. The liturgy was developed into a distinct musical genre
